# Null-section circuits cannot be replaced vertically while preserving coverage

This is an exact obstruction to a proposed GROUPWISE promotion. It is
above the OC target and is not an OC counterexample. It retains actual
Tukey contacts and an actual maximal lattice-free projected container.

Fix d>=2 and let B be a centered unit Euclidean d-ball of volume V.
First take C=[0,1]^2 times B. The mixed set has four unit-ball fibers.
Every source's mixed depth equals its own ball depth by a finite tilt
isolating its binary vertex. Thus the mixed maximum is V/2.

At raw level Q=V, the ambient Tukey projection is precisely the medial
diamond with vertices(1/2,0),(1,1/2),(1/2,1),(0,1/2). The four displayed
points at continuous coordinate0 have depth>=V from a symmetric pair
of fibers. Conversely, outside that diamond there is a binary vertex v
whose affine Hamming-distance function q_v has value s<1/2. The cap

    u.x >= [q_v(z)-s]/(1-s),      ||u||=1,

through the point at continuous coordinate0 captures less than V from
v and zero elsewhere. Continuous reflection and convexity reduce any
other continuous coordinate to0. This proves the exact projection.
The ambient region is full dimensional; for example the inverse-tail
compactness argument in the companion actual-facet note gives a small
continuous ball above the barycenter of any three binary bases, and
the edge midpoint contacts span the base plane.

The split L={0<=z_2<=1} is maximal lattice-free and contains this
projection, touching it on its lower facet at p=(1/2,0). Set Y=(p,0).
For a unit continuous u and M>2 define

    H_1={u.x-2z_1-Mz_2>=-1},
    H_2={-u.x+2z_1-Mz_2>=1}.                           (1)

Each has mass exactly Q=V and boundary through Y. H_1 captures only
the whole00 ball; H_2 captures only the whole10 ball. The traces on
these two bottom fibers are supporting at the relevant extrema, and
the top fibers are strictly empty. Thus ALL derivative sections have
H_(d-1) measure zero. Both caps support the ACTUAL Tukey body: shifting
either boundary inward by any sufficiently small positive amount loses
positive mass from its captured whole ball and adds no mass elsewhere.
A point strictly inside the original cap is therefore outside the
level-V depth body. The common contact is genuine, not auxiliary.

Their continuous normals form a positive two-cap circuit. Adding their
margins gives the group's exact projected exterior

    G={z_2<=0}.

The group covers the ENTIRE continuous space over G, and its assigned
bottom fibers have total mass2V. No vertical halfspace that preserves
this coverage can have mass<=Q=V: it must contain both00 and10 and
therefore captures at least2V. The same is true if one only asks to
preserve coverage of S intersect(H_1 union H_2), because that set already
contains both full bottom fibers.

Reflecting(1) across z_2=1/2 gives a top group with the same properties.
The two groups cover S, their projected exteriors are precisely the
exteriors of the maximal split, and every individual cap has massQ.
Both groups are null-section groups. Yet

    M_total=4V > 2Q.

Consequently the proposed replacement of each null group's cost by1
in M_total<=Q[(m-k)/Gamma_d+k] is false: here m=k=2. This is a complete
shared-cover obstruction, not an isolated bad basin assignment.

## Full continuous rank does not repair the obstruction

At the same lower contact take d+1 continuous normals

    u_i=e_i (1<=i<=d),       u_(d+1)=-sum_i e_i,

with equal positive circuit weights. Choose integer coefficients

    a_i=-2 (1<=i<=d),       a_(d+1)=2d,

and a common M>=4d+4. Use caps

    u_j.x+a_j(z_1-1/2)-M z_2>=0.                       (2)

The first d caps capture only the whole00 ball, and the last captures
only the whole10 ball; all top fibers are empty. Every cap has massV,
every section is null, and the continuous circuit has rank d. Since
sum u_j=sum a_j=0, the projected exterior is again G={z_2<=0}.

These also support the actual depth body. Its diamond projection gives
|z_1-1/2|<=z_2. The proper cap w.x-2||w||z_2>=0 through Y has massV
and positive bottom section mass; inward translation decreases mass.
Consequently every depth-V point satisfies w.x<=2||w||z_2. For(2),
therefore, its margin is at most

    [2||u_j||+|a_j|-M]z_2<=0.

Thus the full-rank circuit retains the actual-contact support condition.
Use its reflected top circuit to obtain the same complete two-group
failure of the proposed saturated-group cost1 bound.

## Strict no-heavy one-group variant

Add a ball rB at integer base(2,1), with 0<epsilon=r^d<1/2, and take
the convex hull with the original C. Its actual fibers are exactly the
four original unit balls and the added small ball: every generating
radius is at most1 and only the new exposed base has first coordinate2.
The total is(4+epsilon)V, so every fiber is strictly smaller than one
quarter of the total. The mixed maximum is(1/2+epsilon)V<V, attained
uniquely at the center above(1,1): the exposed bases isolate own caps,
and the three top-line balls give the elementary reflected-endpoint
identity. This is the reflected version of the companion tiny-fiber
construction's exact depth proof.

For the bottom pair(1), take M>3+r. Both caps exclude the added ball,
retain massV, and still support the actual depth body by inward
translation. The contact Y has depth exactly V from the unchanged
symmetric bottom pair and either cap. The actual projected depth body
still lies in the maximal split0<=z_2<=1; it is full dimensional since
adding measure preserves the old level-V region. All null-section and
coverage statements for that bottom group remain exact. Thus even
strict no-heavy volumes do not permit its budget-preserving vertical
replacement.

For full-rank version(2) in this enlarged body, take M>=8d+8. The proper
caps used above still give w.x<=2||w||z_2. The supporting bottom caps
with coefficients +/-2 and layer penalty4 exclude the added small ball;
adding their opposite-continuous-normal pairs gives
|z_1-1/2|<=2z_2 for every level-V point. Hence each margin in(2) is at
most[2||u_j||+2|a_j|-M]z_2<=0. Its first d caps and last cap exclude the
new ball and retain the same full/empty allocations. Thus strict
no-heavy, full-rank circuits also fail vertical replacement.

A vertical cap merely CONTAINING Y can have massV, by isolating one
bottom base. It loses the other bottom fiber and hence does not replace
the group in its actual cover. That weaker statement must not be
substituted for the false coverage-preserving claim refuted here.
